moat_against: Pure commodity price taker — no pricing power
Reserves deplete; must be replaced via capex/exploration/M&A
Rising all-in sustaining costs (H1 2026 AISC +13% YoY per company reports)
Jurisdictional risk — Tarkwa (Ghana) leases expire April 2027, renewal terms unresolved
moat_for: Cost-curve position at Salares Norte (low AISC, steady state reached 2025)
Portfolio of long-life mines across five countries
Scale: ~2.4-2.6 Moz/yr attributable production guidance for 2026
Reserve replacement track record incl. Gold Road acquisition (2025)
moat_justification: Gold miner and pure price taker: no pricing power, no switching costs, product is a commodity. Only moat-like traits are cost-curve position (Salares Norte AISC well below group average as it reached steady state in 2025) and a portfolio of long-life mines across diversified jurisdictions (Australia, Ghana, South Africa, Peru, Chile) plus the Windfall project in Canada. Against: reserves deplete every year and must be replaced by exploration, acquisition or capex; group AISC is rising with industry cost inflation; jurisdictional risk is live (Tarkwa mining leases in Ghana expire April 2027 and renewal terms are still under negotiation); Windfall permitting has been delayed. Earnings are a leveraged function of the gold price, which the company does not control.
name: Gold Fields Limited
one_liner: Price-taking gold miner, moat 3/10 — does not clear 15% on the engine's FY2022-24 median base (weighted IRR 4.0%, IV@15 $4.06 vs $35.59 price; clears 15% only below ~$4.06). That base predates the FY2025 gold-price surge in the engine's data, so this D is a stale-base result, not a read on current earnings power.
